display_title: [XLA] Fix ragged-dot expansion for batched group_sizes layouts

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Fix ragged-dot expansion for batched group_sizes layouts

RaggedDotRewriter expands a ragged-dot by inserting a group dimension into
the operand and masking out the rows of the other groups.  Inserting that
dimension at `new_dim_index` moves every original dimension `d` of the
operand to `d >= new_dim_index ? d + 1 : d`, but the expansion only applied
that shift in some of the places that need it, so two valid ragged-dots
produced invalid HLO:

- A batch dimension that is not the leading one.  The group_sizes broadcast
  mapped the group_sizes dimensions onto the output dimensions 0..rank-1,
  which assumes the batch dimensions come first.  For

    lhs      = f32[64,2,16], lhs_batch_dims={1}, lhs_ragged_dims={0}
    rhs      = f32[3,2,16,8], rhs_batch_dims={1}, rhs_group_dims={0}
    group_sizes = s32[2,3]

  the expansion emitted broadcast(s32[2,3]) -> s32[64,3,2,16] with
  dimensions={0,1}, mapping a size-2 dimension onto a size-64 one, which the
  verifier rejects.

- A flat [G] group_sizes with batch dimensions.  `new_dim_index` was derived
  from the rank of group_sizes, which assumes it carries a batch prefix.
  With a rank-1 group_sizes and a batch dimension it collapsed to 0 and
  collided with the batch dimension, emitting a dot with dimension 0 both
  contracting and batch ("A dimension number is not unique in Dot").

The shift is now a named helper, ShiftedDim(), applied to the group_sizes
broadcast, the iota broadcast and the lhs dimension numbers alike, and
`new_dim_index` is the number of batch dimensions.  group_sizes maps its
batch dimensions onto the operand's batch dimensions and its group dimension
onto the inserted one; a flat [G] broadcasts to the group dimension only,
which matches its meaning of group sizes shared by every batch element.

group_sizes shapes that are neither rank 1 nor [batch..., G] now return
UnimplementedError instead of being miscompiled.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Assign the block-level config in ScanRewriterTriton

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Assign the block-level config in ScanRewriterTriton

`ScanRewriterTriton` created Triton scan fusions without a block-level config,
leaving the tiling to `PriorityFusion` (only when it fuses into the scan) or to
`FusionBlockLevelRewriter` after scheduling.

The pass now assigns the cost model's best tiling when it creates the fusion,
like `SoftmaxRewriterTriton` does, and doesn't rewrite scans that can't be
tiled. This serves the deprecation of `FusionBlockLevelRewriter`.

display_title: PR #52416: [XLA:TSL] Reject sstable block handles past the end of the file

head_commit.message:
PR #52416: [XLA:TSL] Reject sstable block handles past the end of the file

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52416

#ai-generated

**Status quo**: `ReadBlock` allocates `n + kBlockTrailerSize` bytes for the size stored in a `BlockHandle` read from the file, before reading. `Table::Open` (index handle from the footer) and `Table::BlockReader` (data handles from the index block) never compare the handle with the file size.

**Why**: A 48-byte table whose footer names an index block of about 4.4 TB makes `Table::Open` attempt that allocation. TensorFlow checkpoint .index files use this reader: with the stock TensorFlow 2.22.0rc0 CPU wheel, tf.train.load_checkpoint on such a file raises MemoryError (std::bad_alloc) instead of a DataLoss error. This fix was first opened at tensorflow/tensorflow#129998 and redirected here by the TensorFlow maintainer because xla/tsl/lib/io is maintained in openxla/xla.

**Design choices**: Store the file size in `Table::Rep` and add `CheckBlockHandle`, which returns `DataLossError` unless the block and its trailer lie within the file. It runs before the `ReadBlock` calls in `Table::Open` and `Table::BlockReader`, the only callers. `IndexBlockHandlePastEndOfFileIsRejected` and `DataBlockHandlePastEndOfFileIsRejected` record the largest read requested (the size `ReadBlock` allocates) and fail without the `table.cc` change; the full `table_test` passes with it.

**Trade-offs / Alternatives**: Bounding inside `ReadBlock` would need the file size in its public signature; checking at the two callers keeps `format.h` unchanged. The bound is the file size passed to `Table::Open` rather than the footer offset, so any block that lies within the file is still accepted.

AI assistance was used in drafting and validating this change; the patch and tests were reviewed and verified by the author.

Copybara import of the project:

--
cc90438d600c82a5f70be8930ad94876b6207fda by Nathan Keys <professor.moody@pm.me>:

[XLA:TSL] Reject sstable block handles past the end of the file

ReadBlock allocates the block size stored in a BlockHandle before it
reads the block. Table::Open and Table::BlockReader pass it handles read
from the file without comparing them with the file size, so a 48-byte
table can request a buffer of several terabytes.

Store the file size in Table::Rep and reject, with DataLoss, any handle
whose block and trailer do not lie within the file before calling
ReadBlock.

Merging this change closes #52416

[XLA:GPU] Merge PhasedBlockClusterFusion into ThreadBlockSpecializedFusion.

The two emitters are sharing a lot of code already and there are some detail leaking from PhasedBlockCluster emitter to make it horizontally fuseable, so it makes more sense to have a generic emission pipeline.

* HLO fusions can be annotated with both `__thread_block_specialized` and `__phased_block_cluster` fusion kinds to indicate scheduling decisions.
* Emitter supports arbitrary nesting of fusions.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add flag to allow deterministic XLA:GPU ops to read the autotune cache.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add flag to allow deterministic XLA:GPU ops to read the autotune cache.

https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/commit/50c5820fa425ed6006c95bb0c3ddbe7152729c7f disabled reading from the autotune cache whenever `xla_gpu_deterministic_ops` or `xla_gpu_exclude_nondeterministic_ops` is enabled so co-hosted non-deterministic compilations cannot pollute deterministic modules through the shared cache. However, workloads that require preloaded autotune caches break (such as deviceless cudnn).

Add `xla_gpu_experimental_use_autotune_cache_also_for_deterministic_ops` (defaulting to `false`) and gate the deterministic cache bypass in `CreateAutotunerCache` on it. When enabled, deterministic compilations continue to skip online autotuning and cache writes while reading cached configs as before the commit above.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1015455681

display_title: Harden CheckpointReader, BundleReader, TwoLevelIterator, and Block against read errors and corrupt metadata.

head_commit.message:
Harden CheckpointReader, BundleReader, TwoLevelIterator, and Block against read errors and corrupt metadata.

Previously, transient file read errors (such as `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`) or malformed metadata entries during V2 checkpoint scanning could cause `SIGSEGV` or `SIGABRT` crashes:

- `TwoLevelIterator::Next()`, `key()`, and `value()`, as well as `Block::Iter::Next()`, `key()`, and `value()`, now guard against `!Valid()` instead of dereferencing a null `data_iter_` in release builds.
- `Block::Iter` initializes and resets `value_` to `(data_ + restarts_, 0)` so `NextEntryOffset()` never subtracts `data_` from `nullptr`, validates restart offsets against `restarts_` before forming pointers in `Seek()` and `SeekToRestartPoint()`, and uses 64-bit arithmetic in `DecodeEntry()` to prevent 32-bit unsigned integer overflow when checking `(*non_shared + *value_length)`.
- `BundleReader::status()` now propagates `iter_->status()` when `status_` is OK, and `BundleReader::DebugString()` avoids `CHECK`-crashing on invalid iterator states, unparseable `BundleEntryProto` values, or invalid `TensorShapeProto` entries.
- `CheckpointReader::BuildV2VarMaps()` checks `v2_reader_->Valid()` after `Seek(kHeaderEntryKey)` and `v2_reader_->status()` after each pass, replaces `CHECK(entry.ParseFromString(...))`, `TensorSlice(slice_proto)`, `CHECK(filtered_keys.insert(...).second)`, and `TensorShape(entry.shape())` with status-checked builders (`TensorSlice::BuildTensorSlice` and `TensorShape::BuildTensorShape`), and surfaces `DataLossError` via `TF_Status` when `BuildV2VarMaps()` fails without an underlying reader I/O error.

display_title: PR #52416: [XLA:TSL] Reject sstable block handles past the end of the file

head_commit.message:
PR #52416: [XLA:TSL] Reject sstable block handles past the end of the file

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52416

#ai-generated

**Status quo**: `ReadBlock` allocates `n + kBlockTrailerSize` bytes for the size stored in a `BlockHandle` read from the file, before reading. `Table::Open` (index handle from the footer) and `Table::BlockReader` (data handles from the index block) never compare the handle with the file size.

**Why**: A 48-byte table whose footer names an index block of about 4.4 TB makes `Table::Open` attempt that allocation. TensorFlow checkpoint .index files use this reader: with the stock TensorFlow 2.22.0rc0 CPU wheel, tf.train.load_checkpoint on such a file raises MemoryError (std::bad_alloc) instead of a DataLoss error. This fix was first opened at tensorflow/tensorflow#129998 and redirected here by the TensorFlow maintainer because xla/tsl/lib/io is maintained in openxla/xla.

**Design choices**: Store the file size in `Table::Rep` and add `CheckBlockHandle`, which returns `DataLossError` unless the block and its trailer lie within the file. It runs before the `ReadBlock` calls in `Table::Open` and `Table::BlockReader`, the only callers. `IndexBlockHandlePastEndOfFileIsRejected` and `DataBlockHandlePastEndOfFileIsRejected` record the largest read requested (the size `ReadBlock` allocates) and fail without the `table.cc` change; the full `table_test` passes with it.

**Trade-offs / Alternatives**: Bounding inside `ReadBlock` would need the file size in its public signature; checking at the two callers keeps `format.h` unchanged. The bound is the file size passed to `Table::Open` rather than the footer offset, so any block that lies within the file is still accepted.

AI assistance was used in drafting and validating this change; the patch and tests were reviewed and verified by the author.

Copybara import of the project:

--
cc90438d600c82a5f70be8930ad94876b6207fda by Nathan Keys <professor.moody@pm.me>:

[XLA:TSL] Reject sstable block handles past the end of the file

ReadBlock allocates the block size stored in a BlockHandle before it
reads the block. Table::Open and Table::BlockReader pass it handles read
from the file without comparing them with the file size, so a 48-byte
table can request a buffer of several terabytes.

Store the file size in Table::Rep and reject, with DataLoss, any handle
whose block and trailer do not lie within the file before calling
ReadBlock.

Merging this change closes #52416

Lower `kMinDevicelessCudnnVersion` to cuDNN 9.15

Some users (e.g. Waymo's `car_gpu` config) still build with `--define=use_legacy_cudnn=1`, which selects cuDNN 9.15 for all CUDA 13 versions. With the 9.23 floor, deviceless cuDNN compilation is refused for them, so AOT compilation of models with cuDNN fusions or custom calls fails.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Clear loop-dependent dynamic slice configs in autotuning candidates.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Clear loop-dependent dynamic slice configs in autotuning candidates.

`DynamicSliceAnnotator` annotates dynamic slices inside while loops with a
`DynamicSliceConfig` that computes the slice offset from the loop iteration
instead of the offset operands. When the autotuner extracts an instruction into
a standalone module, that loop no longer exists, so the runtime silently uses
iteration 0 and ignores the offset operands. For a Triton GEMM fusion with a
fused per-layer weight `dynamic-slice`, the cuBLASLt fission reference therefore
always reads the first slice while the Triton candidates read the slice selected
by the (randomly initialized) offset operand. All Triton configs are then
rejected as wrong results, and every rejection produces an expensive host-side
diff report.

Clear loop-dependent `DynamicSliceConfig`s in the module that
`GpuCodegenBackend::Compile` builds for each candidate. Loop-invariant configs
remain valid and are kept, and the original module, e.g. via
`FissionBackend::ApplyConfig`, is unchanged.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/52255

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:CPU] Build one CppGen bitcode per source

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Build one CppGen bitcode per source

### Status quo

`eigen_unary.cc` (atan) is compiled into three bitcode variants (16, 32 and
64-byte vectors) and `expm1.cc` into two. `GetCppGenLibraries` picks one per
target from the CPU features and preferred vector width.

Since atan stopped using Eigen, all variants contain the same function bodies.
The only difference is that SysV x86 builds without AVX-512 pass 512-bit
vectors through a `byval` pointer, which `CreateDirectAdapter` already adapts
and the inliner removes.

### Why

The variants cost build targets, embedded binary size and selection code
without changing the generated kernels. The Eigen names and build flags left
behind are misleading.

### Changes

*   Build `atan_ll` and `expm1_ll` once, with no per-width copts or
    `-mavx512f`. Remove `GetCppGenIrString`, `SelectIrString` and
    `AreEigenIntrinsicsAvailable`.
*   Rename `eigen_unary.{h,cc}` to `atan.{h,cc}` and `EigenAtan` to `Atan`,
    matching `Expm1`, `Sin` and `Cos`. Delete the unregistered `EigenTanh`.
*   Drop the Eigen include and `ArrayMap` from `vector_ops.h`, and
    `-DEIGEN_VECTORIZE_GENERIC` from `cc_to_llvm_ir.bzl`.
*   Collapse the per-width tests onto the single bitcode.
    `AtanHasNoLibmCallsAfterInlining` replaces
    `DefinesAvxAndAvx512EigenAtanF64` and covers every f32 and f64 width on
    AVX2 and AVX-512.

### Verification

Kernel IR after `DefineIntrinsicFunctions` + `RunInlineAndOptPasses` is
byte-identical for every atan and expm1 width on SSE4.2, AVX2 and AVX-512
(512- and 256-bit preference), except the 512-bit widths on AVX-512, which now
go through the adapter. Those have the same instructions, with a dropped
`noundef` on one `fabs` call and two independent bitcasts in swapped order.

### Alternatives

*   Keep the variants and only rename: smaller diff, but keeps the dead
    selection logic.
*   Keep one variant per ABI to avoid `byval` adaptation: AArch64 passes
    512-bit vectors indirectly too, so the adapter stays either way, and it
    costs nothing after inlining.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1015449619

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Fix ragged-dot expansion for batched group_sizes layouts

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Fix ragged-dot expansion for batched group_sizes layouts

RaggedDotRewriter expands a ragged-dot by inserting a group dimension into
the operand and masking out the rows of the other groups.  Inserting that
dimension at `new_dim_index` moves every original dimension `d` of the
operand to `d >= new_dim_index ? d + 1 : d`, but the expansion only applied
that shift in some of the places that need it, so two valid ragged-dots
produced invalid HLO:

- A batch dimension that is not the leading one.  The group_sizes broadcast
  mapped the group_sizes dimensions onto the output dimensions 0..rank-1,
  which assumes the batch dimensions come first.  For

    lhs      = f32[64,2,16], lhs_batch_dims={1}, lhs_ragged_dims={0}
    rhs      = f32[3,2,16,8], rhs_batch_dims={1}, rhs_group_dims={0}
    group_sizes = s32[2,3]

  the expansion emitted broadcast(s32[2,3]) -> s32[64,3,2,16] with
  dimensions={0,1}, mapping a size-2 dimension onto a size-64 one, which the
  verifier rejects.

- A flat [G] group_sizes with batch dimensions.  `new_dim_index` was derived
  from the rank of group_sizes, which assumes it carries a batch prefix.
  With a rank-1 group_sizes and a batch dimension it collapsed to 0 and
  collided with the batch dimension, emitting a dot with dimension 0 both
  contracting and batch ("A dimension number is not unique in Dot").

The shift is now a named helper, ShiftedDim(), applied to the group_sizes
broadcast, the iota broadcast and the lhs dimension numbers alike, and
`new_dim_index` is the number of batch dimensions.  group_sizes maps its
batch dimensions onto the operand's batch dimensions and its group dimension
onto the inserted one; a flat [G] broadcasts to the group dimension only,
which matches its meaning of group sizes shared by every batch element.

group_sizes shapes that are neither rank 1 nor [batch..., G] now return
UnimplementedError instead of being miscompiled.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Clear loop-dependent dynamic slice configs in autotuning candidates.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Clear loop-dependent dynamic slice configs in autotuning candidates.

`DynamicSliceAnnotator` annotates dynamic slices inside while loops with a
`DynamicSliceConfig` that computes the slice offset from the loop iteration
instead of the offset operands. When the autotuner extracts an instruction into
a standalone module, that loop no longer exists, so the runtime silently uses
iteration 0 and ignores the offset operands. For a Triton GEMM fusion with a
fused per-layer weight `dynamic-slice`, the cuBLASLt fission reference therefore
always reads the first slice while the Triton candidates read the slice selected
by the (randomly initialized) offset operand. All Triton configs are then
rejected as wrong results, and every rejection produces an expensive host-side
diff report.

Clear loop-dependent `DynamicSliceConfig`s in the module that
`GpuCodegenBackend::Compile` builds for each candidate. Loop-invariant configs
remain valid and are kept, and the original module, e.g. via
`FissionBackend::ApplyConfig`, is unchanged.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/52255

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1014687114

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Mask all reduced dimensions in single-tile Triton reductions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Mask all reduced dimensions in single-tile Triton reductions.

`EmitReduceWithNoRegion` only masked `reduce_hlo.dimensions()[0]` before
reducing. Now we have multi-dimensional reductions (e.g. `dimensions={0,2}`).
Here, when a later reduced dimension is padded up to a power-of-two tile, the padding lanes were never replaced by the neutral value and leaked into the result whenever the fused computation produced non-neutral values for them (e.g. `exp`, `iota`).

Mask every reduced dimension, matching what `EmitReduceWithRegion` already does.

display_title: PR #51925: Fix a deadlock when communicator is being split from a parent communicator which is being abandoned

head_commit.message:
PR #51925: Fix a deadlock when communicator is being split from a parent communicator which is being abandoned

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51925

📝 Summary of Changes

This CL contains two parts, both are needed to make the test pass reliably.

Deadlock fix:
In AcquireClique, when an existing clique's parent isn't a superset of the new split_from, the callback abandons it. It erases the cache entry while holding the process-wide state.mu. The clique's last shared_ptr (to_lock) was dropped at the end of that lambda, still under state.mu, so the NCCL communicators were destroyed inside the lock. Destroying communicators can block until peers participate. Those peers may be in their own abandon path, waiting for state.mu. The result is a deadlock across ranks.

The abandoned clique is moved into an abandoned variable declared outside the lambda. It is destroyed after state.mu is released. The wait on safety_lock stays under state.mu, because it must wait for any running program and prevent concurrent state changes.

dangling pointer:
 A split clique stored const `GpuClique* parent_`, and `IsParentSupersetOf` dereferenced it to read the parent's key. The abandon logic can destroy the parent while its split children are still cached.
The fix is to store `std::optional<GpuCliqueKey> parent_key_` by value.

This bug has been there for a while but with this unit test, it's easier to surface. I'd suggest to bundle them together in a single PR.

🎯 Justification

deadlock

Pass `filter: blob:none` to `actions/checkout` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` so CI runners only download git blobs needed for the checked-out revision (and any commits checked out by `bazel-diff`). This speeds up git checkout, especially on Windows CI runners.

display_title: PR #51724: [XLA:GPU] Add locality-domain placement to the CUDA device allocator

head_commit.message:
PR #51724: [XLA:GPU] Add locality-domain placement to the CUDA device allocator

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51724

📝 Summary of Changes

Implements the allocator layer that later PRs build the per-domain BFC pools on.

Adds `StreamExecutor::CreateLocalityDomainMemoryAllocator(int locality_domain_id)`, which returns a MemoryAllocator whose physical memory is placed on one locality domain (die) of a multi-die GPU.

CUDA implementation: `locality_domain_id` added to `CudaDeviceAllocator::Options`. When it's set, the allocator creates physical memory with `cuMemCreate` with location set to `CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_DEVICE_LOCALITY_DOMAIN`.

Errors instead of fallback: it rejects out-of-range domain IDs, CUDA older than 13.4, single-domain devices, and the cuMemAlloc path (use_vmm=false). It never falls back to whole-device memory.

🎯 Justification

This is the third PR in the locality-domain series ([first](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50131) and [second](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51429) PRs)

🚀 Kind of Contribution

✨ New Feature and 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

N/A: this PR adds the allocator only. Performance benefits to be evaluated later.

🧪 Unit Tests:
- `CudaDeviceAllocatorLocalityDomainTest.RejectsOutOfRangeLocalityDomain`: domain IDs below -1 or above 255 are rejected.
- `CudaDeviceAllocatorLocalityDomainTest.LocalityDomainRequiresCuda134`: CUDA older than 13.4 is rejected.
- `CudaDeviceAllocatorLocalityDomainTest.LocalityDomainRequiresVmm`: use_vmm=false is rejected.
- `CudaExecutorTest.CreateLocalityDomainMemoryAllocatorRejectsInvalidId`: IDs outside [0, domain_count) are rejected.
- `DeviceAddressVmmAllocatorTest.RejectsLocalityDomainMemorySpaces`: locality-domain colors are rejected on every allocation path.

🧪 Execution Tests:
Both run on a single GPU:

- `CudaDeviceAllocatorLocalityDomainTest.PlacesMemoryOnEachDomain`: for each domain, allocates memory and checks with `cuMemGetAllocationPropertiesFromHandle` that its location is `CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_DEVICE_LOCALITY_DOMAIN` with the requested domain ID. Then it round-trips data host to device to host.
- `CudaExecutorTest.CreateLocalityDomainMemoryAllocatorWorks`: creates an allocator for every domain and allocates from it. On a single-domain GPU, it checks that creating one fails.

display_title: PR #51843: [XLA:GPU] Fix Command Buffer Output Zeroing

head_commit.message:
PR #51843: [XLA:GPU] Fix Command Buffer Output Zeroing

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51843

📝 Summary of Changes

`KernelThunk`, `CustomKernelThunk` and `CuDnnThunk` zero some of their output
buffers before running. All three did this only in `ExecuteOnStream`, via
`stream->MemZero`. Their `Record` paths built argument addresses and then
created exactly one node with nothing in between, so once a thunk was captured
into a command buffer the zeroing was absent from the recorded graph entirely.
`CuDnnThunk` missed it on both branches: the explicit path never zeroed, and the
traced fallback traces only `graph->Execute(...)`, leaving the `MemZero` outside
the captured lambda.

`Record` now records a memset command per zeroed buffer and makes the thunk's own
command depend on them, so ordering is transitively unchanged for anything
downstream. Because buffer addresses move between executions, the memsets must be
updated too, and `Record` is handed back only the single node it returned — so
the memset handles are kept in `CommandStateManager`, keyed by the node they were
recorded alongside. That keying matters: an unrolled while loop records one
command into the same command buffer once per trip, and all those recordings
share a single state object. `CustomCallThunk` and `RaggedAllToAllThunk` use the
same pattern.

The shared logic lives in a new `zeroed_outputs.{h,cc}`. No signature, proto or
emitter changes, and no change to the eager path.

🎯 Justification

This is the default path. `kKernel`/`kCustomKernel` map to `FUSION` and `kCuDnn`
to `CUDNN`, both enabled by default, and `IsConvertible` has no zeroed-outputs
guard. Any Triton/Pallas kernel declaring `zeroed_outputs`, and cuDNN fMHA via
`should_memzero`, silently loses its zeroing once a command buffer forms.

Kernels request zeroed outputs because they accumulate into them rather than
overwriting, and a command buffer replays the same buffers every step, so the
error compounds across iterations. Failure is silent without any error, just a missing
node.

This looks to have been introduced by commit [604cf9e4c0](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/37025), which added `zeroed_output_buffer_indices_` touching
only `ExecuteOnStream`.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

N/A — correctness fix, no performance claim

🧪 Unit Tests:

**`kernel_thunk_test.cc`, `custom_kernel_thunk_test.cc`** — a test
kernel computes `c = a + b` with `a=1, b=2`. These tests zero **`b`**, an input;
zeroing the output `c` proves nothing since the kernel overwrites it. Zeroing
recorded gives `c == 1`, dropped gives `c == 3`.
- `ExecuteOnStreamZeroed` — eager control
- `RecordCommandBufferZeroed`, `RecordCommandBufferUpdateZeroed`
- `RecordCommandBufferTwoRecordingsZeroed` (kernel only) — one thunk recorded
  twice into one command buffer, both updated against moved buffers. This is the
  unrolled-loop shape; a flat memset list leaves the first recording stale.

**`cudnn_thunk_test.cc`** — a probe output the graph never writes, pre-filled

PR #51843: [XLA:GPU] Fix Command Buffer Output Zeroing

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51843

📝 Summary of Changes

`KernelThunk`, `CustomKernelThunk` and `CuDnnThunk` zero some of their output
buffers before running. All three did this only in `ExecuteOnStream`, via
`stream->MemZero`. Their `Record` paths built argument addresses and then
created exactly one node with nothing in between, so once a thunk was captured
into a command buffer the zeroing was absent from the recorded graph entirely.
`CuDnnThunk` missed it on both branches: the explicit path never zeroed, and the
traced fallback traces only `graph->Execute(...)`, leaving the `MemZero` outside
the captured lambda.

`Record` now records a memset command per zeroed buffer and makes the thunk's own
command depend on them, so ordering is transitively unchanged for anything
downstream. Because buffer addresses move between executions, the memsets must be
updated too, and `Record` is handed back only the single node it returned — so
the memset handles are kept in `CommandStateManager`, keyed by the node they were
recorded alongside. That keying matters: an unrolled while loop records one
command into the same command buffer once per trip, and all those recordings
share a single state object. `CustomCallThunk` and `RaggedAllToAllThunk` use the
same pattern.

The shared logic lives in a new `zeroed_outputs.{h,cc}`. No signature, proto or
emitter changes, and no change to the eager path.

🎯 Justification

This is the default path. `kKernel`/`kCustomKernel` map to `FUSION` and `kCuDnn`
to `CUDNN`, both enabled by default, and `IsConvertible` has no zeroed-outputs
guard. Any Triton/Pallas kernel declaring `zeroed_outputs`, and cuDNN fMHA via
`should_memzero`, silently loses its zeroing once a command buffer forms.

Kernels request zeroed outputs because they accumulate into them rather than
overwriting, and a command buffer replays the same buffers every step, so the
error compounds across iterations. Failure is silent without any error, just a missing
node.

This looks to have been introduced by commit [604cf9e4c0](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/37025), which added `zeroed_output_buffer_indices_` touching
only `ExecuteOnStream`.

🐛 Bug Fix

N/A — correctness fix, no performance claim

**`kernel_thunk_test.cc`, `custom_kernel_thunk_test.cc`** — a test
kernel computes `c = a + b` with `a=1, b=2`. These tests zero **`b`**, an input;
zeroing the output `c` proves nothing since the kernel overwrites it. Zeroing
recorded gives `c == 1`, dropped gives `c == 3`.
- `ExecuteOnStreamZeroed` — eager control
- `RecordCommandBufferZeroed`, `RecordCommandBufferUpdateZeroed`
- `RecordCommandBufferTwoRecordingsZeroed` (kernel only) — one thunk recorded
  twice into one command buffer, both updated against moved buffers. This is the
  unrolled-loop shape; a flat memset list leaves the first recording stale.

**`cudnn_thunk_test.cc`** — a probe output the graph never writes, pre-filled
with `0xdeadbeef`: zeroed reads 0, dropped reads the sentinel.
`CuDnnThunkZeroedTest.{ExecuteOnStream, RecordCreateReplayAndUpdate}`,
parameterized over the explicit and traced branches — both fail without the fix,
for different reasons.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Mask all reduced dimensions in single-tile Triton reductions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Mask all reduced dimensions in single-tile Triton reductions.

`EmitReduceWithNoRegion` only masked `reduce_hlo.dimensions()[0]` before
reducing. Now we have multi-dimensional reductions (e.g. `dimensions={0,2}`).
Here, when a later reduced dimension is padded up to a power-of-two tile, the padding lanes were never replaced by the neutral value and leaked into the result whenever the fused computation produced non-neutral values for them (e.g. `exp`, `iota`).

Mask every reduced dimension, matching what `EmitReduceWithRegion` already does.

name: CI
display_title: Block scaled and structured sparse matmuls need extra operands (scales,

head_commit.message:
Block scaled and structured sparse matmuls need extra operands (scales,
zero points, sparsity indices) next to lhs and rhs. A separate opcode
keeps kDot a plain binary op and lets backends rewrite the extended form
early.

kDotGeneral takes lhs, rhs and at least one metadata operand, with dot
dimension numbers, a SparsityConfig and a BlockScalingConfig. It reuses
the existing HloInstructionProto fields. The verifier rejects a
dot-general without metadata operands; a plain dot must stay a kDot.

TensorBlockScalingConfig gains an optional per dimension block_sizes field
to support padded scale use-cases.

display_title: PR #52416: [XLA:TSL] Reject sstable block handles past the end of the file

head_commit.message:
PR #52416: [XLA:TSL] Reject sstable block handles past the end of the file

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52416

#ai-generated

**Status quo**: `ReadBlock` allocates `n + kBlockTrailerSize` bytes for the size stored in a `BlockHandle` read from the file, before reading. `Table::Open` (index handle from the footer) and `Table::BlockReader` (data handles from the index block) never compare the handle with the file size.

**Why**: A 48-byte table whose footer names an index block of about 4.4 TB makes `Table::Open` attempt that allocation. TensorFlow checkpoint .index files use this reader: with the stock TensorFlow 2.22.0rc0 CPU wheel, tf.train.load_checkpoint on such a file raises MemoryError (std::bad_alloc) instead of a DataLoss error. This fix was first opened at tensorflow/tensorflow#129998 and redirected here by the TensorFlow maintainer because xla/tsl/lib/io is maintained in openxla/xla.

**Design choices**: Store the file size in `Table::Rep` and add `CheckBlockHandle`, which returns `DataLossError` unless the block and its trailer lie within the file. It runs before the `ReadBlock` calls in `Table::Open` and `Table::BlockReader`, the only callers. `IndexBlockHandlePastEndOfFileIsRejected` and `DataBlockHandlePastEndOfFileIsRejected` record the largest read requested (the size `ReadBlock` allocates) and fail without the `table.cc` change; the full `table_test` passes with it.

**Trade-offs / Alternatives**: Bounding inside `ReadBlock` would need the file size in its public signature; checking at the two callers keeps `format.h` unchanged. The bound is the file size passed to `Table::Open` rather than the footer offset, so any block that lies within the file is still accepted.

AI assistance was used in drafting and validating this change; the patch and tests were reviewed and verified by the author.

cc90438d600c82a5f70be8930ad94876b6207fda by Nathan Keys <professor.moody@pm.me>:

[XLA:TSL] Reject sstable block handles past the end of the file

ReadBlock allocates the block size stored in a BlockHandle before it
reads the block. Table::Open and Table::BlockReader pass it handles read
from the file without comparing them with the file size, so a 48-byte
table can request a buffer of several terabytes.

Store the file size in Table::Rep and reject, with DataLoss, any handle
whose block and trailer do not lie within the file before calling
ReadBlock.

Merging this change closes #52416

display_title: PR #51724: [XLA:GPU] Add locality-domain placement to the CUDA device allocator

head_commit.message:
PR #51724: [XLA:GPU] Add locality-domain placement to the CUDA device allocator

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51724

📝 Summary of Changes

Implements the allocator layer that later PRs build the per-domain BFC pools on.

Adds `StreamExecutor::CreateLocalityDomainMemoryAllocator(int locality_domain_id)`, which returns a MemoryAllocator whose physical memory is placed on one locality domain (die) of a multi-die GPU.

CUDA implementation: `locality_domain_id` added to `CudaDeviceAllocator::Options`. When it's set, the allocator creates physical memory with `cuMemCreate` with location set to `CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_DEVICE_LOCALITY_DOMAIN`.

Errors instead of fallback: it rejects out-of-range domain IDs, CUDA older than 13.4, single-domain devices, and the cuMemAlloc path (use_vmm=false). It never falls back to whole-device memory.

🎯 Justification

This is the third PR in the locality-domain series ([first](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50131) and [second](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51429) PRs)

🚀 Kind of Contribution

✨ New Feature and 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

N/A: this PR adds the allocator only. Performance benefits to be evaluated later.

🧪 Unit Tests:
- `CudaDeviceAllocatorLocalityDomainTest.RejectsOutOfRangeLocalityDomain`: domain IDs below -1 or above 255 are rejected.
- `CudaDeviceAllocatorLocalityDomainTest.LocalityDomainRequiresCuda134`: CUDA older than 13.4 is rejected.
- `CudaDeviceAllocatorLocalityDomainTest.LocalityDomainRequiresVmm`: use_vmm=false is rejected.
- `CudaExecutorTest.CreateLocalityDomainMemoryAllocatorRejectsInvalidId`: IDs outside [0, domain_count) are rejected.
- `DeviceAddressVmmAllocatorTest.RejectsLocalityDomainMemorySpaces`: locality-domain colors are rejected on every allocation path.

🧪 Execution Tests:
Both run on a single GPU:

- `CudaDeviceAllocatorLocalityDomainTest.PlacesMemoryOnEachDomain`: for each domain, allocates memory and checks with `cuMemGetAllocationPropertiesFromHandle` that its location is `CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_DEVICE_LOCALITY_DOMAIN` with the requested domain ID. Then it round-trips data host to device to host.
- `CudaExecutorTest.CreateLocalityDomainMemoryAllocatorWorks`: creates an allocator for every domain and allocates from it. On a single-domain GPU, it checks that creating one fails.

display_title: Block scaled and structured sparse matmuls need extra operands (scales,

head_commit.message:
Block scaled and structured sparse matmuls need extra operands (scales,
zero points, sparsity indices) next to lhs and rhs. A separate opcode
keeps kDot a plain binary op and lets backends rewrite the extended form
early.

kDotGeneral takes lhs, rhs and at least one metadata operand, with dot
dimension numbers, a SparsityConfig and a BlockScalingConfig. It reuses
the existing HloInstructionProto fields. The verifier rejects a
dot-general without metadata operands; a plain dot must stay a kDot.

TensorBlockScalingConfig gains an optional per dimension block_sizes field
to support padded scale use-cases.

name: CI
display_title: Allow deserializing cuDNN graphs compiled for GPUs with fewer SMs

head_commit.message:
Allow deserializing cuDNN graphs compiled for GPUs with fewer SMs

cuDNN's handle-based execution plan deserialization requires an exact match on
`multiProcessorCount`, so AOT plans for a smaller-SM SKU or MIG partition fail
to load on a GPU of the same architecture with more SMs.

To support this, we serialize the target's SM count and cuDNN's
`DeviceProperties` JSON into `CudnnThunkProto` at compile time and pass them to
`DnnSupport::DeserializeGraph`. The JSON stays opaque to XLA: when the target
has fewer SMs than the attached GPU (`GpuExecutable` already rejects compute
capability mismatches),
`CudnnSupport::DeserializeGraph` deserializes the compile-time
`DeviceProperties`, finalizes the plan against those properties via
`graph.set_device_properties()`, and runs warmup on the handle (keeping same-SM
loads on the existing handle path).

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Skip `SimpleAddSubWithPMSampling` when CUPTI returns `CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED`

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Skip `SimpleAddSubWithPMSampling` when CUPTI returns `CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED`

`CuptiPmSamplerDevice::SetConfig()` configures PM sampling with `CUPTI_PM_SAMPLING_TRIGGER_MODE_GPU_TIME_INTERVAL`, which CUPTI supports only on GA10x and newer architectures and rejects with `CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED` on GA100 (A100).

Map `CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED` to `absl::UnimplementedError` in `ToStatus(CUptiResult)`, and update `SimpleAddSubWithProfilerTest` to `GTEST_SKIP()` when `CuptiTracer::Enable()` returns `Unimplemented` (alongside `PermissionDenied`) and `ASSERT_OK` otherwise.

display_title: Exclude manual targets in bazel-diff cquery options

head_commit.message:
Exclude manual targets in bazel-diff cquery options

`Build.bazel_command` appends `-manual` to `--build_tag_filters` when running with `--target_pattern_file`, but `bazel_diff.get_cquery_command_options` passed `build.build_tag_filters` unchanged. On CPU presubmit builds (whose tag filters only contain negative tags), `bazel cquery` attempted to configure `tags = ["manual"]` targets under `//build_tools/...:all-targets`.

Therefore this change appends `-manual` to `--build_tag_filters` in `get_cquery_command_options` so `bazel-diff` `cquery` matches the test execution tag filters.

name: CI
display_title: Avoid unconditional filter mask creation in ConvolutionGroupConverter

head_commit.message:
Avoid unconditional filter mask creation in ConvolutionGroupConverter

`ConvolutionVisitor::HandleConvolution` previously called `ExpandedFilterShape`
and `GetExpandedFilterMask` before checking whether filter expansion would
actually be used (`group_size == 1 && (!is_cost_viable_ || filter_expansion_)`).
When `group_size > 1` or `filter_expansion_ == false`, this emitted dead mask
instructions and materialized `group_count * group_size` elements in host memory
via `GetMaskIds`, overflowing 32-bit `int` loop counters or exhausting memory on
large feature dimensions.

Move `ExpandedFilterShape` and `GetExpandedFilterMask` into the filter-expansion
branch and widen the loop counters in `GetMaskIds` to `int64_t`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1015286921

name: CI
display_title: Unify CppGen `atan` intrinsics and strip stack-protector attributes.

head_commit.message:
Unify CppGen `atan` intrinsics and strip stack-protector attributes.

Under `-DEIGEN_VECTORIZE_GENERIC`, Eigen's clang `PacketMath` backend defines only a single packet size (`EIGEN_GENERIC_VECTOR_SIZE_BYTES`), causing narrower sub-packet vector intrinsics (`atan.v4f32` and `atan.v2f64` in 32-byte bitcode; `atan.v4f32`, `atan.v8f32`, `atan.v2f64`, and `atan.v4f64` in 64-byte bitcode) to fall back to scalar libm `atanf`/`atan` calls and scalar `atan.f64` to emit `@copysign`. Additionally, the unused `xla.unused.tanh.*` entry points in `eigen_unary.cc` bloated the embedded bitcode and emitted external `@fma` calls from scalar `Eigen::internal::pmadd` under `EIGEN_SCALAR_MADD_USE_FMA=1`.

Replace the scalar and Eigen-dispatched `atan` implementations in `eigen_unary.cc` with a single `Atan<T>` template function (`HornerPoly`, `BitwiseAbs`, `BitwiseCopysign`) shared across scalars and all vector widths (`v4f32`, `v8f32`, `v16f32`, `v2f64`, `v4f64`, `v8f64`), and remove the unused `xla.unused.tanh.*` entry points from `eigen_unary.{h,cc}`. In `cpp_gen_intrinsics.cc` and `cc_to_llvm_ir.bzl`, mark `CreateDirectAdapter` wrappers for always-inlining, strip stack-protector and stack-probe attributes in `LinkIntoModule` so `AlwaysInlinerPass` does not merge them into callers, and pass `-fno-exceptions -fno-unwind-tables -fno-asynchronous-unwind-tables -fno-stack-protector` when compiling CppGen bitcode.

name: CI
display_title: Avoid unconditional filter mask creation in ConvolutionGroupConverter

head_commit.message:
Avoid unconditional filter mask creation in ConvolutionGroupConverter

`ConvolutionVisitor::HandleConvolution` previously called `ExpandedFilterShape`
and `GetExpandedFilterMask` before checking whether filter expansion would
actually be used (`group_size == 1 && (!is_cost_viable_ || filter_expansion_)`).
When `group_size > 1` or `filter_expansion_ == false`, this emitted dead mask
instructions and materialized `group_count * group_size` elements in host memory
via `GetMaskIds`, overflowing 32-bit `int` loop counters or exhausting memory on
large feature dimensions.

Move `ExpandedFilterShape` and `GetExpandedFilterMask` into the filter-expansion
branch and widen the loop counters in `GetMaskIds` to `int64_t`.

- Updates `SelectKTestParams` and `ApproxTopKSelectKTestParams` in `xla/service/gpu/gpu_compiler_test.cc` to cover the new `k` boundaries for `f32` and `bf16`.

display_title: [IFRT] Add XLA linking through ifrt::Compiler::Compile for pjrt_ifrt

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Add XLA linking through ifrt::Compiler::Compile for pjrt_ifrt

This change adds experimental support for linking PjRtRelocatables
through IFRT via the ifrt::Compiler::Compile API. The basic idea is to
embed the relocatables into the IFRT compile options, and if they're
present, to invoke the linker via the PjRtPhaseCompiler API and ignore
the input module.

This is a little hacky, but avoids any IFRT API updates while
relocatables are still experimental.

As an additional note, this change exposes the GetPjRtCompiler function
as part of the PjRt public API. Normally callers use PjRtCompile, but
in order to invoke the API we really need access to the PjRtCompiler to
get at the PjRtPhaseCompiler. I considered just inlining the logic, but
that seemed worse given that it has been changing somewhat (for example,
with the compiler variants changes).

display_title: `LookThroughForAllReduce` previously stepped through arbitrary chains of `kConvert` instructions alongside `kReshape`, `kPad`, and `kSlice` formatting operations. Meanwhile, `AllReduceReassociate::RunImpl` only checked `reassociate_converted_ar_` and `AreCompatibleConverts` when `MatchOperandsToAllReduceWithOptionalConvert` matched a single direct `kConvert` on each operand.

head_commit.message:
`LookThroughForAllReduce` previously stepped through arbitrary chains of `kConvert` instructions alongside `kReshape`, `kPad`, and `kSlice` formatting operations. Meanwhile, `AllReduceReassociate::RunImpl` only checked `reassociate_converted_ar_` and `AreCompatibleConverts` when `MatchOperandsToAllReduceWithOptionalConvert` matched a single direct `kConvert` on each operand.

When an operand chained multiple `kConvert` instructions or combined `kConvert` with formatting operations, `RunImpl` hoisted `kAllReduce` past narrowing casts unchecked.

Return a `LookThroughResult` struct from `LookThroughForAllReduce`, matching a direct single user `kConvert` of `kAllReduce` only when `reassociate_converted_ar_` is enabled. Track `has_formatting` on `kReshape`, `kPad`, and `kSlice` chains, reject mixed `kConvert` and formatting operands, and remove `MatchOperandsToAllReduceWithOptionalConvert` and `OptionalConvertWithOneUser`.

name: CI
display_title: Linearize small staged async H2D transfers inline in CommonPjRtClient.

head_commit.message:
Linearize small staged async H2D transfers inline in CommonPjRtClient.

For `kImmutableUntilTransferCompletes` transfers, `LinearizeIntoImpl` always
dispatched the linearize + H2D copy to `async_work_runner()`, even when the
staging buffer was already available. That extra thread hop per tensor
exposes multi-host synchronous steps to work-queue tail latency.

Run linearization inline when the buffer is <= 512 KiB and the staging buffer
is already available; larger or throttled transfers still go through
`async_work_runner()`.

Measured on a 256-chip TPU training job (8 input tensors, 264 KiB per chip per
step), together with a companion change in the Pathways transport layer:
stalls >= 25s went from 11 in 4,200 steps (max 118s) to 0, and steady-state
throughput went from ~105 to ~145 steps/min (+30-40%).

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Bounds-check scan, scatter and collective-permute protos

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Bounds-check scan, scatter and collective-permute protos

HloInstruction::CreateFromProto indexes repeated proto fields and tuple
shapes without checking their sizes in three cases, so a malformed
HloModuleProto reads or writes out of bounds before the verifier runs:

- kScan reads dimensions(0) without checking that dimensions is
  non-empty.
- kScatter indexes the operand vector at operand_count / 2, which
  dereferences an empty vector when there are no operands.
- In-place collective-permute reads operands 0, 2 and 3, the
  start-indices tuple and dynamic_slice_sizes without checking their
  sizes; two of the four slice-size reads use CHECK_GE, which still
  admits proto_index == size. When input buffers have different numbers
  of offset tuples, slice_sizes is sized from the first buffer only and
  the loop writes past its end. That last case is reached by a module
  that HloVerifier accepts.

Return an error for each case, using the constraints that the parser,
ShapeInference and HloVerifier already enforce, and size slice_sizes by
the total number of offset tuples.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Reject index_vector_dim as a gather/scatter batching dim

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reject index_vector_dim as a gather/scatter batching dim

ValidateGatherDimensionNumbers and ValidateScatterDimensionNumbers check
each start_indices_batching_dims / scatter_indices_batching_dims entry
against the indices shape with the implicit trailing index vector dim
appended, and do not reject an entry equal to index_vector_dim. The
StableHLO spec forbids it (gather C15, scatter C16). A module that
passes HloVerifier can therefore name the index vector dim as a
batching dim, either an explicit index_vector_dim or the implicit one
equal to the indices rank.

Code that maps batching dims while skipping index_vector_dim does not
expect this. GatherExpander and ScatterExpander dereference a null
instruction in MakeBroadcastHlo, and the AlgebraicSimplifier gather(pad)
rewrite reads past the padding config or throws from .at().

Return InvalidArgument from both validators when a batching dim equals
index_vector_dim. Add tests for the explicit and implicit forms and for
batching dims before, after and at the last real dim of the indices.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Compile CUDA command buffer helper kernels as C++ device symbols

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Compile CUDA command buffer helper kernels as C++ device symbols

## Problem
CUDA command buffer helper kernels (`set_case_condition`,
`set_while_condition`, and `noop`) were embedded as `.target sm_50` PTX
strings. On first conditional command buffer recording per device, the CUDA
driver JIT compiled that PTX on the single thread `cuda_driver` pool. That
JIT stalled first recording by 187 ms on `sm_103a` and serialized subsequent
devices on the same host.

## Change
Compile these helpers as CUDA C++ kernels in `command_buffer_kernels.cu.cc`
and load them via `KernelLoaderSpec::CreateInProcessSymbolSpec`. Minimum
compile time CUDA toolkits already exceed CUDA 12.3, so the legacy PTX
workaround is unnecessary. Cache loaded helper kernels per `StreamExecutor` as
a `Resource` instead of reloading per `CudaCommandBuffer`, and destroy
resources in `~CudaExecutor` before checking live kernel maps. Program
behavior is unchanged and no flags change. Helper loading now resolves via
`cudaGetFuncBySymbol` and bypasses the `cuda_driver` pool, which stays size 1
for residual PTX loads.

Tests:
- `//xla/stream_executor/cuda:cuda_command_buffer_test`: symbol specs and case.
- `//xla/stream_executor/cuda:cuda_executor_test`: cached kernel teardown.

name: CI
display_title: Wake waiting threads in FIFO order in xla::Semaphore::Acquire.

head_commit.message:
Wake waiting threads in FIFO order in xla::Semaphore::Acquire.

When a multi-model TPU inference server is under heavy concurrency and hits its
max in-flight computation limit (`max_inflight_computations_semaphore_`),
incoming requests block on `xla::Semaphore::Acquire`. Because `Acquire` waited
on `absl::Mutex::LockWhen` without tracking arrival order, releasing capacity
woke arbitrary waiting threads rather than the oldest waiting request, allowing
newly arrived requests to repeatedly jump ahead of older requests and causing
severe tail-latency starvation.

Track blocked callers in a singly-linked FIFO queue of stack-allocated `Waiter`
nodes (`head_` / `tail_`) with per-waiter `absl::CondVar`. Capacity returned in
`Release` is handed off directly to queued waiters in arrival order, and
`TryAcquire` avoids barging ahead of queued waiters (`head_ == nullptr`) while
allowing smaller acquisitions to bypass earlier unsatisfied larger requests.

Tested with `bazel test //xla/pjrt:semaphore_test`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1014141776

display_title: Propagate Read errors in tsl::Read*Proto

head_commit.message:
Propagate Read errors in tsl::Read*Proto

Record non-EOF `RandomAccessFile::Read` errors stickily in `FileStream::Next()` while preserving `OutOfRangeError` on empty EOF reads, propagate `stream->non_eof_status()` after `ReadBinaryProto` and `ReadTextProto` succeed so lazy-open `NotFoundError` (e.g. on `gs://` files) is not swallowed as a valid empty proto, and only fall back to binary parsing in `ReadTextOrBinaryProto` on `DataLoss` / `OutOfRange` parse failures so real I/O errors propagate directly.

name: CI
display_title: Dynamically scale chunked PJRT host-device transfer pipeline depth from 4 to 8.

head_commit.message:
Dynamically scale chunked PJRT host-device transfer pipeline depth from 4 to 8.

With 2 MiB chunks, a static 4-stage pipeline (8 MiB ring buffer) underutilizes host transpose threads and PCIe DMA concurrency on multi-core TPU hosts for single-tensor transfers and synchronous `kImmutableOnlyDuringCall` transfers, whereas a static 8-stage pipeline increases staging ring buffer memory pressure and worker thread contention when multiple asynchronous transfers run concurrently.

Track active chunked H2D and D2H `PipelinedChunkedTransfer` instances via `PipelinedChunkedTransfer::ActiveCount(is_h2d)` in `xla/pjrt/common_pjrt_client.cc` and select `max_stages = (!sync && ActiveCount(is_h2d) > 0) ? kBaseStages : kMaxStages` (4 when concurrent async transfers are in flight, 8 for single transfers or synchronous `kImmutableOnlyDuringCall` transfers). If concurrent async transfers arrive while an 8-stage transfer is in flight, `CompleteStage2Chunk` drains its active stages down to `kBaseStages = 4`.

Updated `ChunkedLinearizeAndDelinearizeRoundTrip` in `xla/pjrt/pjrt_client_test.cc` to use 4096-row shapes (> 16 MiB) to exercise 8-stage ring buffer wrap-around, and verified CPU and TPU PJRT unit test suites. On TPU v7x and TPU v6e 8-vCPU host-device transfer benchmarks across `nt = 1, 4, 8`, single-transfer (`nt = 1`) and synchronous `kImmutableOnlyDuringCall` throughput improves by 18%–58% on TPU v7x (e.g., 64 MiB F32 H2D 21.7 → 34.3 GB/s, H2D sync 22.1 → 34.8 GB/s, D2H 23.7 → 32.0 GB/s) and by up to 45% on TPU v6e while keeping multi-transfer (`nt = 4, 8`) throughput neutral or faster.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1014093591

head_commit.message:
Remove runtime multi_slice_config from FunctionalHloRunner and add slice discovery to PJRT Megascale extension.

Multi-slice compilation options already carry serialized slice configuration
through `CompileOptions::multi_slice_config`, whereas passing an in-memory
`MultiSliceConfig` pointer via `ExecuteOptions::multi_slice_config` cannot
cross the PJRT C API boundary. Remove `RunningOptions::multi_slice_config`
from `xla/tools/multihost_hlo_runner/functional_hlo_runner.h` and stop
forwarding it in `FunctionalHloRunner::RunInternal`.

Expose `discover_slices`, `multi_slice_config_get_incarnation_id`,
`multi_slice_config_get_local_host_id`, `multi_slice_config_get_num_hosts`,
and `global_barrier` on `PJRT_Megascale_Extension`, and provide corresponding
C API client wrappers (`DiscoverSlices`, `DiscoverSlicesFromClient`,
`GetIncarnationId`, `GetLocalHostId`, `GetNumHosts`, and `GlobalBarrier`)
in `megascale_c_api_client`.

head_commit.message:

name: CI
display_title: Dynamically scale chunked PJRT host-device transfer pipeline depth from 4 to 8.

head_commit.message:
Dynamically scale chunked PJRT host-device transfer pipeline depth from 4 to 8.

With 2 MiB chunks, a static 4-stage pipeline (8 MiB ring buffer) underutilizes host transpose threads and PCIe DMA concurrency on multi-core TPU hosts for single-tensor transfers and synchronous `kImmutableOnlyDuringCall` transfers, whereas a static 8-stage pipeline increases staging ring buffer memory pressure and worker thread contention when multiple asynchronous transfers run concurrently.

Track active chunked H2D and D2H `PipelinedChunkedTransfer` instances via `PipelinedChunkedTransfer::ActiveCount(is_h2d)` in `xla/pjrt/common_pjrt_client.cc` and select `max_stages = (!sync && ActiveCount(is_h2d) > 0) ? kBaseStages : kMaxStages` (4 when concurrent async transfers are in flight, 8 for single transfers or synchronous `kImmutableOnlyDuringCall` transfers). If concurrent async transfers arrive while an 8-stage transfer is in flight, `CompleteStage2Chunk` drains its active stages down to `kBaseStages = 4`.

Updated `ChunkedLinearizeAndDelinearizeRoundTrip` in `xla/pjrt/pjrt_client_test.cc` to use 4096-row shapes (> 16 MiB) to exercise 8-stage ring buffer wrap-around, and verified CPU and TPU PJRT unit test suites. On TPU v7x and TPU v6e 8-vCPU host-device transfer benchmarks across `nt = 1, 4, 8`, single-transfer (`nt = 1`) and synchronous `kImmutableOnlyDuringCall` throughput improves by 18%–58% on TPU v7x (e.g., 64 MiB F32 H2D 21.7 → 34.3 GB/s, H2D sync 22.1 → 34.8 GB/s, D2H 23.7 → 32.0 GB/s) and by up to 45% on TPU v6e while keeping multi-transfer (`nt = 4, 8`) throughput neutral or faster.

display_title: [XLA] Add `tile_padding` option to `TransposePlan`

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Add `tile_padding` option to `TransposePlan`

Add an optional `tile_padding` byte setting to `TransposePlan::Options`. When set, `Execute()` and `ExecuteChunk()` set the padding bytes in the output buffer, rather than requiring callers to pre-fill the entire destination buffer before transposing.

Each chunk initializes the padding bytes within its own slice of the output, so padding work runs in parallel across threads alongside the transpose without touching valid element slots.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Fuse identical-window collective-permutes on paired (hi, lo) operands in CollectivePermuteCSE.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Fuse identical-window collective-permutes on paired (hi, lo) operands in CollectivePermuteCSE.

When `xla_enable_enzyme_comms_opt` is enabled and 64-bit floating-point values are decomposed into `(hi, lo)` pairs (via `X64SplitLow`/`X64SplitHigh`, `FastTwoSum`/`TwoSum`, or adjacent tuple elements), halo exchanges emit two `collective-permute` instructions with identical `source_target_pairs` and slice windows on the paired `hi` and `lo` arrays. Teach `CollectivePermuteCSE` to concatenate the two sliced operands along dimension 0, issue a single array `collective-permute`, and slice the result back into the `hi` and `lo` halves.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Split stacked MoveToHost dynamic-update-slices in HostOffloadLegalize.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Split stacked MoveToHost dynamic-update-slices in HostOffloadLegalize.

When `jax.lax.scan(..., unroll > 1)` stacks `MoveToHost`-annotated outputs from each unrolled body iteration, it lowers to `MoveToHost -> bitcast -> concatenate` (or `TpuConcatDecomposer` `pad + maximum/add/or` tree) `-> bitcast -> dynamic-update-slice` into the scan output buffer. Because `HostOffloader` only recognizes `MoveToHost` feeding `dynamic-update-slice` through unary bitcast/reshape/copy instructions, it treated the intermediate `concatenate` / `pad+maximum` and `dynamic-update-slice` as host compute (`_xla_compute_type="host"`), which lowered to synchronous CPU `host-call`s.

Decompose a `dynamic-update-slice` whose update operand is a concatenation (or `pad + maximum/add/or` tree) of `MoveToHost` slices into sequential per-slice `dynamic-update-slice` instructions in `HostOffloadLegalize` so each `MoveToHost` feeds its own `dynamic-update-slice` directly and lowers to an asynchronous host DMA.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1015605975

display_title: [XLA] Flatten control-flow subcomputations in CollectivePipeliner.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Flatten control-flow subcomputations in CollectivePipeliner.

Loop peeling and rotation in `CollectivePipeliner` previously only cloned direct `while` subcomputations one level deep, leaving `conditional` branches and nested control-flow subtrees with multiple callers and triggering a `CHECK` failure in `HloAliasAnalysis` (`caller_callsites().size() == 1`).

Replace the 1-level `while` cloning with `FlattenCallGraph(FlattenCallGraph::SkipCloningForCalls)` at the end of `RunPipeliner` so `while` and `conditional` subtrees are flattened recursively while preserving shared `call` targets on non-flat graphs.

display_title: [XLA:TSL] Bound record lengths in RecordReader

head_commit.message:
[XLA:TSL] Bound record lengths in RecordReader

RecordReader::GetMetadata and SkipRecords added a file-supplied record
length to the footer size and stream offset without a bound, so a length
near 2^64 wrapped and a bogus record was counted. ReadRecord on a
Snappy-compressed file passed a length above INT64_MAX to
SnappyInputStream::ReadNBytes as a negative count, which crashed the
reader. Return DataLoss in all three when the record would extend past
INT64_MAX.

Add tests for each case, with genuine-record controls.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Exclude thread-local allocations from memory usage report

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Exclude thread-local allocations from memory usage report

In XLA `BufferAssigner`, `GatherComputationsByAllocationType` classifies
`to_apply` subcomputations attached to ops such as `reduce`, `sort`, `map`, and
`custom-call` as `is_thread_local`. `AssignBuffersForThreadLocalComputations`
still creates logical `BufferAllocation` records for values inside those
subcomputations, but they bypass `HeapSimulator` and are never materialized in
global device memory.

For `reduce`/`sort`/`map` scalar bodies these records are only a few bytes, but
for host-offload `custom-call`s (`custom_call_target="HostExecute"`,
`to_apply=%host_computation`) the subcomputation parameters can be full
tensors, causing `GetMemoryUsageReportProto()` (`memory-usage-report.txt`) to
over-report `color=0` device memory by gigabytes. Skipping
`allocation.is_thread_local()` aligns `MemoryUsageReport()` with
`ComputeTotalAllocationBytes()` and backend buffer allocators.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1015811221

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Exclude thread-local allocations from memory usage report

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Exclude thread-local allocations from memory usage report

In XLA `BufferAssigner`, `GatherComputationsByAllocationType` classifies
`to_apply` subcomputations attached to ops such as `reduce`, `sort`, `map`, and
`custom-call` as `is_thread_local`. `AssignBuffersForThreadLocalComputations`
still creates logical `BufferAllocation` records for values inside those
subcomputations, but they bypass `HeapSimulator` and are never materialized in
global device memory.

For `reduce`/`sort`/`map` scalar bodies these records are only a few bytes, but
for host-offload `custom-call`s (`custom_call_target="HostExecute"`,
`to_apply=%host_computation`) the subcomputation parameters can be full
tensors, causing `GetMemoryUsageReportProto()` (`memory-usage-report.txt`) to
over-report `color=0` device memory by gigabytes. Skipping
`allocation.is_thread_local()` aligns `MemoryUsageReport()` with
`ComputeTotalAllocationBytes()` and backend buffer allocators.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1011001087

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Add `tile_padding` option to `TransposePlan`

Add an optional `tile_padding` byte setting to `TransposePlan::Options`. When set, `Execute()` and `ExecuteChunk()` set the padding bytes in the output buffer, rather than requiring callers to pre-fill the entire destination buffer before transposing.

Each chunk initializes the padding bytes within its own slice of the output, so padding work runs in parallel across threads alongside the transpose without touching valid element slots.

display_title: [XLA] Fuse identical-window collective-permutes on paired (hi, lo) operands in CollectivePermuteCSE.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Fuse identical-window collective-permutes on paired (hi, lo) operands in CollectivePermuteCSE.

When `xla_enable_enzyme_comms_opt` is enabled and 64-bit floating-point values are decomposed into `(hi, lo)` pairs (via `X64SplitLow`/`X64SplitHigh`, `FastTwoSum`/`TwoSum`, or adjacent tuple elements), halo exchanges emit two `collective-permute` instructions with identical `source_target_pairs` and slice windows on the paired `hi` and `lo` arrays. Teach `CollectivePermuteCSE` to concatenate the two sliced operands along dimension 0, issue a single array `collective-permute`, and slice the result back into the `hi` and `lo` halves.

Restrict multi page buffer assignment to Color(0)

Previously, setting `HloModuleConfig::page_size_kib() > 0` partitioned both
`Color(0)` and `Color(1)` temporary allocations into fixed size pages and

buffer interval comparator.

name: CI
display_title: Linearize small staged async H2D transfers inline in CommonPjRtClient.

head_commit.message:
Linearize small staged async H2D transfers inline in CommonPjRtClient.

For `kImmutableUntilTransferCompletes` transfers, `LinearizeIntoImpl` always
dispatched the linearize + H2D copy to `async_work_runner()`, even when the
staging buffer was already available. That extra thread hop per tensor
exposes multi-host synchronous steps to work-queue tail latency.

Run linearization inline when the buffer is <= 512 KiB and the staging buffer
is already available; larger or throttled transfers still go through
`async_work_runner()`.

Measured on a 256-chip TPU training job (8 input tensors, 264 KiB per chip per
step), together with a companion change in the Pathways transport layer:
stalls >= 25s went from 11 in 4,200 steps (max 118s) to 0, and steady-state
throughput went from ~105 to ~145 steps/min (+30-40%).

name: CI
display_title: Add DeserializeLoadedExecutable RPC to IFRT Proxy

head_commit.message:
Add DeserializeLoadedExecutable RPC to IFRT Proxy

Adds a new IfrtRequest/IfrtResponse pair so a client can load a serialized
executable on the server backend.

Client: Compiler::DeserializeLoadedExecutable uploads the bytes through the
host buffer store, sends the request, and builds the executable from the
CompileResponse. It rejects host callbacks and load options of any type other
than XlaDeserializeExecutableOptions with an Unimplemented error.

Server: IfrtBackend handles the request on the compile thread pool, waits for
the uploaded bytes, calls the default Compiler, and returns the same
CompileResponse as Compile. The Compile response code is now shared.

The previous Unimplemented error cited an unstable serialization format. That is
not a concern here: the proxy never reads the bytes and sends them unchanged.
The server backend that loads them checks that they match its own runtime and
returns an error status if they do not. The same compatibility rule applies to
any IFRT client that loads a serialized executable.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1015743319

name: CI
display_title: PR #52256: Prevent copies in async computations by propagating constraints onto async roots

head_commit.message:
PR #52256: Prevent copies in async computations by propagating constraints onto async roots

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52256

📝 Summary of Changes

`LayoutAssignment` can currently insert copies into async HloComputations that must contain only parameter instructions and a root. This causes the output HLO to fail verification (the HLO verifier requires async computations to contain only parameter instructions and a root).

This PR modifies constraint propagation logic to prevent copies inside async computations. When propagating constraints into async computations, incoming constraints on parameters are redirected to the root's corresponding operands. Incoming constraints on the async computation's result are already attached to the async root. Existing constraint negotiation logic will select a consistent set of constraints for the root. The selected root operand constraints will then propagate mandatorily to the parameters. This ensures that there are no layout mismatches inside the async body, and forces mismatches to be handled by copies before async-start or after async-done.

The new redirection, mandatory parameter propagation, and forced interface refresh apply to main-thread async computations that currently contain only parameters and a root, as identified by `IsSingleInstructionAsyncComputation`.

**Implementation details**

There are four main parts to this change:

1. In `PropagateAcrossEdge`, redirect constraints targeting an eligible async parameter to every root operand position that uses it. Preserve existing mandatory operand constraints. Existing tuple operand constraints are also preserved because operand layout negotiation currently only handles arrays.
2. Stop `AddAsyncDoneConstraints` from resetting the callee's result interface to match caller requirements. Instead, constrain async-done to the callee's result layout; existing copy insertion handles conflicting caller uses or entry results. Callers can still influence the body earlier through `HloDataflowPropagation::Run`.
3. In `PropagateUseConstraintToDefs`, make propagation from the eligible async root to parameters of the same computation mandatory. This lets the root's accepted operand requirement replace a conflicting parameter buffer constraint, even at equal or higher existing priority.
4. In `CalculateComputationLayout`, refresh an eligible async computation's own interface from its current parameter/root buffer constraints on every call, including later rounds and equal-priority updates. Otherwise, a change after the first calculation can leave the stored interface stale.

**Alternative implementations considered**

1. Post pass legalization: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51372

   - Run constraint propagation as usual, then identify async bodies with extra instructions and wrap them in an async computation whose root is a `kCall` into the original computation.
   - Pros: directly repairs the single-instruction-body violation without changing layout selection; leaves already-valid bodies unchanged.
   - Cons: introduces another computation/call and repairs invalid HLO after producing it. The reviewer preferred preventing invalid bodies in the first place.

2. Defensive copies on inputs / outputs of async-start / async-done.

   - Pros: Minimal change to underlying constraint propagation logic.
   - Cons: This can introduce unnecessary copies. Consider an async computation with caller input/output requirements {0,1} and a flexible body could use {0,1} throughout. Isolating its layout choices using defensive copies can instead produce:

     input {0,1} -> copy to {1,0} -> async-start -> body using {1,0} -> async-done -> copy to {0,1} -> caller use

     Propagating the caller's requirements into the flexible body can avoid both copies.

3. Detect and resolve async mismatches in `AssignLayouts`.

   - When finalization would insert an operand or root copy inside an async body, reconcile its parameter/result layouts and insert any necessary copies at the caller instead.
   - Pros: keeps propagation largely unchanged and handles conflicts at the point where copies would otherwise be inserted.
   - Cons: changing body layouts at this stage also requires updating the stored interface, async chain shapes, and caller requirements after propagation has finished. This design also mixes responsibilities between the different parts of the code responsible for constraint propagation vs finalization / copy insertion.

**Limitations**

This PR does not resolve incompatible fixed requirements on repeated uses of the same parameter. A single parameter cannot satisfy both operand layouts in this example:

```
body {
  p = f32[2,3]{1,0} parameter(0)
  ROOT op = f32[2,3]{1,0} custom-call(p, p), custom_call_target="test",
    operand_layout_constraints={f32[2,3]{0,1}, f32[2,3]{1,0}}
}
```

A follow-up PR is planned to split parameters with incompatible uses and update the async-start arguments, allowing separate caller copies for those uses.

Copies inserted earlier by `PrepareHloForLayoutAssignment`, such as for sends or certain aliased custom calls, are also outside this change. Such bodies already contain extra instructions before the new propagation logic runs and do not match the shared predicate.

🎯 Justification

Currently, valid input HLO containing async computations can become invalid during layout assignment, causing subsequent HLO verification to fail compilation. The added tests include HLO that triggers this issue.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests

- Added layout-sensitive HLO verification at the end of these existing tests to reject extra instructions inside restricted async bodies and check layout consistency:

  - `AsyncStartDoneMandatoryConstraints`
  - `AsyncStartDoneTupleMandatoryConstraints`
  - `AsyncStartPreservesMandatoryCallerParameterLayout`
  - `AsyncStartPreservesMandatoryCallerParameterLayoutMultipleOperands`
  - `AsyncStartPreservesMandatoryCallerCustomCallLayout`
  - `PropagateAsyncStartConstraintIntoUnconstrainedWrappedComputation`

  The last test also checks that no copies are inserted when the flexible elementwise root can satisfy agreeing caller requirements.

- `AsyncDoneEntryRootLayoutMismatch`: a fixed custom-call result conflicts with the entry result layout; checks that the copy becomes the entry root after async-done.
- `AsyncDoneCallerOperandLayoutMismatch`: a fixed custom-call result conflicts with a caller consumer's operand requirement; checks that the copy is between async-done and that consumer.
- `PropagateAsyncDoneComputationConstraintIntoUnconstrainedWrappedComputation`: a layout requirement on an async-done due to the entry computation layout propagates into the flexible wrapped computation with no copies inserted.
- `PropagateAsyncDoneUseConstraintIntoUnconstrainedWrappedComputation`: a layout requirement on an async-done due to a subsequent use by a custom call propagates into the flexible wrapped computation with no copies inserted.
- `AsyncStartPropagatesLayoutsToReorderedAndRepeatedParameterUses`: distinct caller input layouts propagate to reordered and repeated root operands without copies.
- `AsyncRootOverridesHigherPriorityParameterConstraint`: a test subclass adds a conflicting high-priority parameter constraint; checks that mandatory root-to-parameter propagation replaces it without copies.
- `AsyncComputationWithWhileRoot`: Ensures that modified layout assignment works for a more complicated example where a while op is the root of an async computation.

🧪 Execution Tests

Execution tests with 3 different MaxText recipes across 1–2 GB300 nodes show no meaningful changes in performance or final loss. Furthermore, the HLO after optimization and thunk sequences are identical between baseline and test runs for all three recipes.

The recipes below use the same training args and XLA flags as described [here](https://gist.github.com/rao-ashish/4d01922faf917d7c341c61cdb6a8e3f5). However, the baseline uses XLA commit `f824cdd4dc`, before both commits in this PR; the test uses `efb9ac2815`. Both use the same JAX revision (`70b48fe198`) and MaxText revision (`d068d3383b`).

| model_name | variant_name | num_gpus | last_10_steps_median_tflops_per_sec | final_loss |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| llama3-8b | baseline | 4 (1 nodes) | 1371.268549 | 0.106671 |
| llama3-8b | test | 4 (1 nodes) | 1371.452575 | 0.106375 |
| gemma3-27b | baseline | 8 (2 nodes) | 1188.412046 | 0.131652 |
| gemma3-27b | test | 8 (2 nodes) | 1186.615610 | 0.131538 |
| mixtral-8x7b | baseline | 8 (2 nodes) | 367.914525 | 7.588028 |
| mixtral-8x7b | test | 8 (2 nodes) | 367.607860 | 7.589622 |

name: CI
display_title: Add DeserializeLoadedExecutable RPC to IFRT Proxy

head_commit.message:
Add DeserializeLoadedExecutable RPC to IFRT Proxy

Adds a new IfrtRequest/IfrtResponse pair so a client can load a serialized
executable on the server backend.

Client: Compiler::DeserializeLoadedExecutable uploads the bytes through the
host buffer store, sends the request, and builds the executable from the
CompileResponse. It rejects host callbacks and load options of any type other
than XlaDeserializeExecutableOptions with an Unimplemented error.

Server: IfrtBackend handles the request on the compile thread pool, waits for
the uploaded bytes, calls the default Compiler, and returns the same
CompileResponse as Compile. The Compile response code is now shared.

The previous Unimplemented error cited an unstable serialization format. That is
not a concern here: the proxy never reads the bytes and sends them unchanged.
The server backend that loads them checks that they match its own runtime and
returns an error status if they do not. The same compatibility rule applies to
any IFRT client that loads a serialized executable.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1000592516

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:HLO] Fold constant divisors and rewrite division by broadcasted sqrt to rsqrt in AlgebraicSimplifier.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:HLO] Fold constant divisors and rewrite division by broadcasted sqrt to rsqrt in AlgebraicSimplifier.

1. Fold division by constant:
   - Matches m::Constant, m::Broadcast(m::Constant), m::Convert(m::Constant),
     and m::Broadcast(m::Convert(m::Constant)).
   - Removes m::NonConstant dividend constraint, allowing 1.0 / Const to directly
     fold into inverted constant literals without generating intermediate multiplications.
   - Converts literal types when dividing across differing element types.

2. Rewrite division by broadcasted (r)sqrt:
   - A / broadcast(sqrt(B)) => A * broadcast(rsqrt(B))
   - A / broadcast(rsqrt(B)) => A * broadcast(sqrt(B))
   - When A == 1, directly replaces the division with the broadcasted (r)sqrt.
   - Recovers 1.28x speedup on RMSNorm f32[16, 1024] (8.59 µs -> 6.69 µs) and 1.13x
     on f32[1024, 4096] (575.9 µs -> 508.0 µs).

display_title: Add two disabled reproduction tests to `xla/backends/profiler/gpu/cupti_tracer_test.cc` (with CUDA graph helpers in `xla/backends/profiler/gpu/cuda_test.h` and `xla/backends/profiler/gpu/cuda_test.cu.cc`) covering CUPTI `cuptiFinalize()` failures when profiling CUDA graphs:

head_commit.message:
Add two disabled reproduction tests to `xla/backends/profiler/gpu/cupti_tracer_test.cc` (with CUDA graph helpers in `xla/backends/profiler/gpu/cuda_test.h` and `xla/backends/profiler/gpu/cuda_test.cu.cc`) covering CUPTI `cuptiFinalize()` failures when profiling CUDA graphs:

1. `CuptiTracerTest.DISABLED_GraphTraceWithCuptiFinalizeCrashesOnPostSessionGraphLaunch`: captures and instantiates a CUDA graph before profiling, launches it during a `CuptiTracer` session with `CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_GRAPH_TRACE` and `cupti_finalize = true`, and launches it again after `Disable()` calls `cuptiFinalize()`, reproducing `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` (700) on the post-session graph launch.
2. `CuptiTracerTest.DISABLED_ConcurrentConditionalGraphUpdateWithCuptiFinalizeFails`: builds a parent CUDA graph containing a conditional IF node (`cudaGraphNodeTypeConditional`) whose body contains a child graph node that is continuously recaptured (`cudaStreamBeginCaptureToGraph`) and updated (`cudaGraphExecChildGraphNodeSetParams`) and launched on a worker thread while `CuptiTracer` runs profiling sessions with `CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_CONCURRENT_KERNEL` (without `CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_GRAPH_TRACE`) and `cupti_finalize = true`, reproducing `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` (700) / `cudaErrorLaunchFailure` (719) or driver lock hangs.

Both tests are prefixed with `DISABLED_` so the test target passes by default in CI, while running manually with `--test_arg=--gunit_also_run_disabled_tests` (or `--test_arg=--gtest_also_run_disabled_tests` in OSS) reproduces the failures.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Take shared GPU lock when checking warm-up redzones in GpuProfiler.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Take shared GPU lock when checking warm-up redzones in GpuProfiler.

Acquire a shared `ReaderMutexLock` on `GetGpuMutex(stream_executor_)` before
calling `warmup_rz->CheckRedzones()` in `GpuProfiler::Profile`, matching
`GpuProfiler::CheckInputBuffers` and `GpuProfiler::CheckOutputBuffer`. This
prevents host-side CUDA calls and redzone check kernels in `CheckRedzones()`
from overlapping with timed profiling runs on other threads during parallel autotuning.

display_title: Propagate Read errors in tsl::Read*Proto

head_commit.message:
Propagate Read errors in tsl::Read*Proto

Record non-EOF `RandomAccessFile::Read` errors stickily in `FileStream::Next()` while preserving `OutOfRangeError` on empty EOF reads, propagate `stream->non_eof_status()` after `ReadBinaryProto` and `ReadTextProto` succeed so lazy-open `NotFoundError` (e.g. on `gs://` files) is not swallowed as a valid empty proto, and only fall back to binary parsing in `ReadTextOrBinaryProto` on `DataLoss` / `OutOfRange` parse failures so real I/O errors propagate directly.
