https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/commit/50c5820fa425ed6006c95bb0c3ddbe7152729c7f disabled reading from the autotune cache whenever `xla_gpu_deterministic_ops` or `xla_gpu_exclude_nondeterministic_ops` is enabled so co-hosted non-deterministic compilations cannot pollute deterministic modules through the shared cache. However, workloads that require preloaded autotune caches break (such as deviceless cudnn).

Add `xla_gpu_experimental_use_autotune_cache_also_for_deterministic_ops` (defaulting to `false`) and gate the deterministic cache bypass in `CreateAutotunerCache` on it. When enabled, deterministic compilations continue to skip online autotuning and cache writes while reading cached configs as before the commit above.

name: CI
display_title: Fix GPU integer `tf.math.pow` mismatch with CPU/NumPy for exponents >= 64.

head_commit.message:
Fix GPU integer `tf.math.pow` mismatch with CPU/NumPy for exponents >= 64.

Previously, the MLIR-generated GPU `Pow` kernel lowered `stablehlo.power` to a Linalg/SCF exponentiation-by-squaring loop with a hardcoded upper bound of 6 iterations, which only inspected the lowest 6 bits of the exponent (`y % 64`) and discarded bits at positions >= 6. As a result, odd bases with exponents >= 64 (such as `(-47)**66`) and even bases with exponents >= 64 produced incorrect results on GPU compared to CPU and NumPy fixed-width two's-complement wrap-around semantics.

Update the integer `Pow` exponentiation-by-squaring loop upper bound from 6 to the integer element bit-width so all exponent bits are processed.

Fixes #118202

display_title: Add two disabled reproduction tests to `xla/backends/profiler/gpu/cupti_tracer_test.cc` (with CUDA graph helpers in `xla/backends/profiler/gpu/cuda_test.h` and `xla/backends/profiler/gpu/cuda_test.cu.cc`) covering CUPTI `cuptiFinalize()` failures when profiling CUDA graphs:

head_commit.message:
Add two disabled reproduction tests to `xla/backends/profiler/gpu/cupti_tracer_test.cc` (with CUDA graph helpers in `xla/backends/profiler/gpu/cuda_test.h` and `xla/backends/profiler/gpu/cuda_test.cu.cc`) covering CUPTI `cuptiFinalize()` failures when profiling CUDA graphs:

1. `CuptiTracerTest.DISABLED_GraphTraceWithCuptiFinalizeCrashesOnPostSessionGraphLaunch`: captures and instantiates a CUDA graph before profiling, launches it during a `CuptiTracer` session with `CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_GRAPH_TRACE` and `cupti_finalize = true`, and launches it again after `Disable()` calls `cuptiFinalize()`, reproducing `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` (700) on the post-session graph launch.
2. `CuptiTracerTest.DISABLED_ConcurrentConditionalGraphUpdateWithCuptiFinalizeFails`: builds a parent CUDA graph containing a conditional IF node (`cudaGraphNodeTypeConditional`) whose body contains a child graph node that is continuously recaptured (`cudaStreamBeginCaptureToGraph`) and updated (`cudaGraphExecChildGraphNodeSetParams`) and launched on a worker thread while `CuptiTracer` runs profiling sessions with `CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_CONCURRENT_KERNEL` (without `CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_GRAPH_TRACE`) and `cupti_finalize = true`, reproducing `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` (700) / `cudaErrorLaunchFailure` (719) or driver lock hangs.

Both tests are prefixed with `DISABLED_` so the test target passes by default in CI, while running manually with `--test_arg=--gunit_also_run_disabled_tests` (or `--test_arg=--gtest_also_run_disabled_tests` in OSS) reproduces the failures.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Isolate SparseCore offloads in the HLO isolator

Detect SparseCore modules by the async chain their main thread starts on the
`sparsecore` thread. Such modules are never defused, use the interpreter as
their only reference, skip when the reference returns `Unimplemented`, and
report a mismatch without a fusion debugger rerun. Also expose
`SparseCoreOffloadSkipReason` to skip units with RNG, Mosaic kernels, or no
SparseCore work.

display_title: jaxlib: Add relocatables support

head_commit.message:
jaxlib: Add relocatables support

This change adds a PyRelocatable (which wraps a PjRtRelocatable) and
APIs to PyClient for producing and consuming them. Under the hood,
relocatables are a PjRt abstraction with no IFRT counterpart until
they're more stable. Relocatables can only be constructed via the
PjRtPhaseCompiler API, but they can be consumed by the linker via
ifrt::Compiler::Compile, which has clandestine support for that path
(structured this way to avoid adding new APIs).

display_title: [IFRT] Add XLA linking through ifrt::Compiler::Compile for pjrt_ifrt

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Add XLA linking through ifrt::Compiler::Compile for pjrt_ifrt

This change adds experimental support for linking PjRtRelocatables
through IFRT via the ifrt::Compiler::Compile API. The basic idea is to
embed the relocatables into the IFRT compile options, and if they're
present, to invoke the linker via the PjRtPhaseCompiler API and ignore
the input module.

This is a little hacky, but avoids any IFRT API updates while
relocatables are still experimental.

As an additional note, this change exposes the GetPjRtCompiler function
as part of the PjRt public API. Normally callers use PjRtCompile, but
in order to invoke the API we really need access to the PjRtCompiler to
get at the PjRtPhaseCompiler. I considered just inlining the logic, but
that seemed worse given that it has been changing somewhat (for example,
with the compiler variants changes).

Update llvm18_linux_x86_64 to llvm22_linux_x86_64 in MODULE.bazel

`build_tools/ci/BUILD` resolves `@llvm_linux_x86_64//:version.bzl` to construct the `@llvm<version>_linux_x86_64` repository name for `//build_tools/ci:clang_tidy_bin`. After the `rules_ml_toolchain` upgrade to LLVM 22, `_LLVM_REPO_NAME` evaluates to `llvm22_linux_x86_64`, while `MODULE.bazel` still imported `llvm18_linux_x86_64`.

Updating `use_repo` in `MODULE.bazel` to `llvm22_linux_x86_64` fixes configuring `//build_tools/ci/...` under Bzlmod.

display_title: [ROCm] Profile non-foldable ops at the default opt level on ROCm

head_commit.message:
[ROCm] Profile ops at the default opt level with one element per lane.

At O0, ocml functions that ops like sine lower to stay unoptimized
out-of-line calls that spill to the stack, which made gfx950 sine about 14x
slower. Measure at the default opt level and keep O0 only for chains that
LLVM folds above it: integer add, subtract and multiply, and round. Give each
lane its own element so LLVM does not move uniform integer work to the
scalar unit.

display_title: In `PartitionConvolutionTiledOutput`, `ReshardAsWindowedInput` runs on `lhs` and returns `dynamic_slice_index_on_output` ordered by `lhs` dimensions. When a base dilated convolution has permuted spatial and feature or batch dimensions between `lhs` and the output (such as `b0f_0io->bf0` after `TransposeFolding` or `01fb_01io->b01f`) and requires a per shard output window alignment slice, passing `dynamic_slice_index_on_output` directly to `CreateDynamicSlice` on `sharded_conv` applies the spatial slice offset to the wrong output dimension.

head_commit.message:
In `PartitionConvolutionTiledOutput`, `ReshardAsWindowedInput` runs on `lhs` and returns `dynamic_slice_index_on_output` ordered by `lhs` dimensions. When a base dilated convolution has permuted spatial and feature or batch dimensions between `lhs` and the output (such as `b0f_0io->bf0` after `TransposeFolding` or `01fb_01io->b01f`) and requires a per shard output window alignment slice, passing `dynamic_slice_index_on_output` directly to `CreateDynamicSlice` on `sharded_conv` applies the spatial slice offset to the wrong output dimension.

Map `dynamic_slice_index_on_output` from `lhs` dimension order into output dimension order via `input_to_output_indices` before creating the `dynamic-slice` on `sharded_conv`. Existing programs whose `lhs` and output dimensions have identical ordering or do not emit an output alignment slice do not change behavior, with no flag.

`build_tools/ci/BUILD` resolves `@llvm_linux_x86_64//:version.bzl` to construct the `@llvm<version>_linux_x86_64` repository name for `//build_tools/ci:clang_tidy_bin`. name: CI
display_title: [PJRT/JAX] Preserve subnormal floats during JAX Python callbacks on CPU

head_commit.message:
[PJRT/JAX] Preserve subnormal floats during JAX Python callbacks on CPU

When executing CPU computations, PJRT and XLA thread pools configure the CPU to flush subnormal floating-point numbers to zero to improve performance. However, when XLA calls back into Python (via `jax.pure_callback`, `io_callback`, or `buffer_callback`), this setting was left enabled on the calling thread. Python code (like NumPy) expects standard floating-point behavior, so leaving this setting enabled caused subnormal numbers to silently become zero inside user callbacks.

This change adds `tsl::port::ScopedDontFlushDenormal` and `tsl::port::ScopedSetRound(FE_TONEAREST)` to `xla::HostCallbackScope`. This ensures all Python callbacks run with standard floating-point settings, and safely restores XLA's expected settings when the callback returns.

Bumps `JAX_IFRT_VERSION_NUMBER` to 85 and adds regression tests guarded by this version.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1015586840

name: CI
display_title: PR #52481: [ROCm profiler] Keep 64-bit correlation ids when joining activities

head_commit.message:
PR #52481: [ROCm profiler] Keep 64-bit correlation ids when joining activities

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52481

## Problem

`ApiActivityInfoExchange` copies each key of `activity_ops_events_map_` into a `uint32_t corr_id` before looking up the matching HIP API event. openxla/xla#47225 widened correlation ids and these maps to `uint64_t`, the width of `rocprofiler_correlation_id_t::internal`, but missed this local.

For an id at or above 2^32, the lookup uses the truncated value and finds no API event, so every activity row under that id is dropped as "Could not find the counterpart HIP API", and the drop is logged with the truncated id. rocprofiler-sdk hands out internal ids from one process-wide 64-bit counter, so this only shows up after a process has used more than 2^32 ids. I have not seen it in a real trace; the unit test below reproduces it.

## Change

- `const uint32_t corr_id` -> `const uint64_t corr_id` in `ApiActivityInfoExchange`.
- `TestAddKernelEventAndExport` now uses correlation id 2^32 + 42. On the old code the kernel row is dropped and the GPU plane has no lines.

`rocm_collector_test` and `rocm_tracer_test_amdgpu_any` pass on MI355X.
Copybara import of the project:

--
04ef503c121fef4601a89b31b138b18a1ddf2c3e by cj401-amd <chunyjin@amd.com>:

[ROCm profiler] Keep 64-bit correlation ids when joining activities

ApiActivityInfoExchange copied each activity map key into a uint32_t
before looking up its API event. The maps are keyed by uint64_t, the
width of rocprofiler_correlation_id_t::internal, so an id above 2^32
missed its API event and its activity rows were dropped.

TestAddKernelEventAndExport now uses an id above 2^32.

Merging this change closes #52481

head_commit.message:
Document why bazel-diff is disabled on Hermetic ROCm CI build

`XLA_LINUX_X86_GPU_HERMETIC_ROCM_GITHUB_ACTIONS` is a compile-only RBE build with high remote cache hit rates. Running two `bazel cquery` passes for `bazel-diff` adds more overhead than incremental target selection saves, so set `use_bazel_diff=False` explicitly and document the rationale.

display_title: Lower `kMinDevicelessCudnnVersion` to cuDNN 9.15

head_commit.message:
Lower `kMinDevicelessCudnnVersion` to cuDNN 9.15

Some users still build with `--define=use_legacy_cudnn=1`, which selects cuDNN 9.15 for all CUDA 13 versions. With the 9.23 floor, deviceless cuDNN compilation is refused for them, so AOT compilation of models with cuDNN fusions or custom calls fails.

Deviceless compilation stays best effort on older versions, as it already was.

Small while loops hoisted by SmallWhileLoopHoistingPass are now compiled by
emitting the thunks of the loop as usual. Their kernels are linked into one host
kernel that takes disjoint buffer regions as noalias parameters. This replaces
the last use of the legacy IrEmitter for nested computations.
